cards.hearing: You may hear that the Fed just raised interest rates, the first move like this in a while.
cards.why: The Fed sets short-term interest rates, and that ripples into things like credit cards, car loans, and mortgages, so borrowing can cost a little more for a while.
cards.but: But rate moves are part of a normal cycle, not a reason to rewrite a plan built for many years.
cards.story: Picture adjusting the thermostat a notch because the weather shifted. You do not renovate the whole house over one degree. You just dress for it and keep living your life.
say: We expected the Fed to move eventually, and your plan already accounts for that.
One rate decision does not change the years ahead of you.

cards.hearing: You may hear that oil prices jumped this morning, tied to a security scare involving a UK air base.
cards.why: Oil feeds into gas and diesel, so a jump like this can eventually show up at the pump and in what it costs to ship groceries and goods.
cards.but: But headlines about overseas tension come and go, and a single morning's oil move is not a forecast for the year.
cards.story: Think of a driver who sees one red light and decides the whole road trip is ruined. One light does not cancel the trip. You slow down, then keep going.
say: We watch headlines like this without letting them steer the whole plan.
A jump in oil this morning is noise we expect to see from time to time.

cards.hearing: You may hear that stock futures are a little softer this morning after stocks rose on Friday.
cards.why: A quieter, choppier morning like this can feel unsettling, especially right after a good week, but it is a completely normal part of investing.
cards.but: But this kind of back-and-forth is exactly why we build plans for years, not for any single morning.
cards.story: Picture a hiker checking the trail app every five minutes. The trail does not change because you keep refreshing. You look up, keep walking, and you get where you are going.
say: Stocks rose on Friday, and this morning is just a little quieter. That is normal.
We do not chase every morning move. We stick with your plan.
